hypothesis: Among sunflower capitula of one species, the parastichy numbers (Fibonacci pairs such as 34/55, 55/89, 89/144) increase systematically with head size, so heads of different diameter fall into different parastichy pairs.
pass_criterion: Among heads with a measurable size and a Fibonacci parastichy count, Spearman rho between head size (diameter, or the best available size proxy) and the larger parastichy number is >= 0.5 (p<0.01). The median size must also rise across successive Fibonacci pairs. At least 3 distinct pairs, each with n>=5, must be observed, e.g. 34/55, 55/89 and 89/144.
fail_criterion: Spearman rho < 0.2, or the median size does not rise monotonically across the Fibonacci pairs, or fewer than 3 distinct pairs with n>=5 are observed, so that the number does not vary with size.
interpretation: Thompson's "arrangement" means the parastichy (spiral) counts in the clockwise and anticlockwise directions. "Size of the entire structure" means capitulum diameter. The data are citizen-science counts on annotated seedhead photographs. If no diameter field is recorded, a size proxy (e.g. seed count, or pixel width scaled by any reference object) must be used and declared before analysis. This is a modern reinterpretation; if neither is available, the test is undecidable and must not count as a pass. The dataset is mostly of Helianthus annuus cultivars, so "one species" is satisfied only loosely. Cultivar identity may confound the result and should be included as a covariate if recorded.

dataset.name: Data from: Novel Fibonacci and non-Fibonacci structure in the sunflower: results of a citizen science experiment
dataset.publisher: Dryad (Swinton & Ochu, Royal Society Open Science 2016)
dataset.why_it_fits: It contains per-head clockwise and anticlockwise parastichy counts for 657 sunflowers (MSF007_SunflowerData_20151020_anonymised.xlsx; JS annotations for MSF007_Countdata.xlsx) plus annotated seedhead images. Counts can be cross-tabulated against head size, if the spreadsheet records it. The landing page does not show the column names, so this is unconfirmed until the spreadsheet is opened.
